title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: COMING SUNDAY October 11th | Asheville Mardi Gras Cajun Cookoff 2026
location: Wicked Weed Funkatorium, 147 Coxe Avenue, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Sunday, October 11 | 2-5pm | Wicked Weed Funkatorium | Event Details and Tickets 
Laissez les bon temps rouler! Treat yourself to the flavors of Louisiana cuisine cooked by over 15 professional and home chefs. While filling your belly, Two-step your way to happiness with Asheville’s own 2nd Line band!!! 
Compared to the annual Asheville Mardi Gras parade, the Cajun Cookoff is the second most popular event held by Asheville Mardi Gras. The cookoff brings together chefs who serve samples of their best Cajun and Louisiana-inspired dishes to food lovers from all over Western North Carolina. Eventgoers will get to experience the sweet and savory recipes of home and professional chefs alike and will have the chance to vote on their favorites. A panel of judges will also be evaluating the entries and rating them based on certain criteria. First, second, and third place winners in each category will be announced along with the People’s Choice award. 
The Cajun Cookoff is the biggest fundraiser of the year for AMG. Proceeds go to staging the 2027 Mardi Gras parade in Asheville.In addition to some scrumptious food there will be music and a 50-50 raffle (must be present to win.)$35 in advance for AMG members; $40 in advance for nonmembers; $45 date of event.Bring some cash to buy 50/50 raffle tickets!

title: John Rock Loop Hike
description:
WNC Sierra Club
Join the WNC Sierra Club for a beautiful hike in the Pisgah National Forest. The John Rock Loop hike features around 1,100 feet of elevation gain up to a scenic overlook where we will have a snack and rest. This hike is about 5.9 miles in length and will take us approximately 3-4 hours. Be prepared for elevation gain and creek crossings. Make sure to pack food and water to stay nourished and hydrated! Wear gear that you are comfortable hiking in and good shoes. It is also a good idea to have rain gear just to be safe. If you are feeling unwell and/or have a fever, please help us to keep everyone safe and healthy by waiting for the next outing. Families, friends, and pets are all welcome. An adult must accompany all children. All dogs must remain on a leash and be friendly to all.

Please register using this [Link to John Rock Loop Hike Registration.](https://act.sierraclub.org/events/details?formcampaignid=701Po00002DA0ZMIA1)

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Community Day | The Art of Paper

description:
The Asheville Art Museum invites you to visit for free on Saturday, October 10 between 11am–5pm! Come celebrate the exhibition The Art of Paper with an afternoon of creativity and community engagement—featuring live music, art activities, exhibition tours, and more. 
SCHEDULE OF EVENTS
11am–5pm: Free admission to the Museum, including the featured exhibition, The Art of Paper: Selections of Handmade Paper Works from the Collections of Jordan D. Schnitzer and His Family Foundation.  
11:30am–3:30pm: Live piano in the Windgate Foundation Atrium with Willie Sime.  
noon, 1pm, and 2pm: The Art of Paper 30-minute Express Tours.  
12:30pm, 1:30pm, and 2:30pm: Warp, Weft, and the Grid, 30-minute Express Tours. 
1–4pm: Paperweaving in the Studio – Starting with strips of handmade paper crafted from kudzu vines, participants will create a small weaving inspired by traditional overshot patterns, a popular weave structure used to make coverlets and bed coverings. We will turn our weavings into wearable buttons that highlight the beauty of these two art forms, hand weaving and papermaking. Led by artist Alyssa Sacora of The Patchwork Underground, this drop in experience will expose museum guests to new ways of thinking about materials and craft and provide a hands-on learning experience. Beginners are welcome and encouraged. 
2–2:15pm: Asheville School student dance performance in Explore Asheville Exhibition Hall (level 3), featuring Warp, Weft, and the Grid.  
2:30–3pm, 3:15-3:45pm: Asheville School student dance, poetry, and music performances in The Art of Paper. 
Preregister—let us know you’re coming!

description:
Jazz Brunch is now officially on the schedule for every Saturday here in the taproom! We’re so very excited to introduce our newest free weekly event, open to all ages, family & pet-friendly





If you haven’t experienced Jazz Brunch yet, here’s what you can expect: from the moment the music begins, the taproom fills with that perfect weekend energy… laid-back jazz, fresh brunch plates, great beer, and a room full of people settling in and staying awhile. Friends gather around tables, conversations flow easily, and the rhythm of the music sets the tone for a perfect, easy Saturday. It’s exactly the kind of atmosphere we hoped to create when this idea first came to life!



We’re especially excited to continue working with our house Jazz band, “Four Peanuts”, whose smooth, soulful sound brings everything together. The group explores both original compositions and zesty covers of tunes you may or may not know. The trio features Alex Taub on keyboards, Brennan Dugan on bass, and Joe Enright on drums, and will certainly leave your peanuts salted and boiled to perfection! Their music pairs effortlessly with the relaxed brunch setting, turning an ordinary morning into something memorable. The all-new brunch menu is absolutely something to be excited about! French Broad River Pizza will be serving up a mix of breakfast and lunch favorites designed to pair perfectly with a chill afternoon in the taproom.






Thank you for supporting live music, local artists, and community gatherings here at French Broad River Brewery. We can’t wait to welcome you back to the taproom… brunch plate in one hand, beer in the other, and jazz in the background.


  
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. Just minutes from the Biltmore Estate & Downtown, our taproom is a gathering spot for locals and visitors alike. We regularly host live music and entertainment in our taproom, making French Broad River Brewery a lively hub of local activity. From bluegrass to reggae, there’s always something happening. Check out our Events Page to see what’s coming up next! 
No brewery experience is complete without great food. That’s why we offer French Broad River Pizza, serving up hot, hand-tossed pizzas made to order. title: Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons
description:
Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons
with Carlton Burke 
Satuday, October 10  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core 
Register Here!
  
Since birds are capable of long distance flights and many engage in annual migration rituals, their presence in our area often changes in relation to the seasons of the year. In this class we will discuss the seasonal patterns of southern Appalachian birds and focus on some of the major species and their annual life cycles. As part of this program, there will be a “lab” portion where students will be able to meet some live birds and participate in other hands-on components to deepen the learning. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitat

**Specializing in Astrological Events and Sound Healing Journeys**

🌹As Venus turns retrograde, she begins her ancient journey inward, symbolically descending into the underworld to recover something precious that has been lost, buried, forgotten, or surrendered along the way.
In the mythic story of **Inanna's Descent**, the goddess passes through seven gates on her journey into the underworld. At each threshold, she is asked to remove something she carries until eventually she stands completely stripped of the identity and power she once knew.
Venus retrograde invites a similar inner journey.
**What happens when we remove the layers of who we thought we needed to be?**
Our relationships, desires, values, attractions, creativity and relationship with ourselves can become mirrors during this passage. Old connections may reappear. Forgotten desires may stir. Something we once valued may suddenly feel empty, while something neglected begins calling us home.

title: New Moon Ceremony
description:
Awakening Asheville
### **Walking in Balance**

*Finding Harmony Within Ourselves and Our Relationships*

As the seasons change and the days grow shorter, nature reminds us that life is always seeking balance.
There are times to give and times to receive. Times to speak and times to listen. Times to hold on—and times to let go.
But in the busyness of everyday life, it is easy to lose that balance.

We may give so much to others that we neglect ourselves. We may hold onto responsibilities, expectations, relationships, or old stories long after they have become too heavy to carry.

This New Moon invites us to pause and ask:
**Where in my life am I being called back into balance?**

Join us for our monthly sacred virtual New Moon gathering as we step away from the noise of everyday life and create space to listen within.
Together, we will use meditation, reflection, intention, and shamanic practice to explore where our lives may have moved out of balance—and what small changes might help us return to a place of greater harmony.

This month's journey will consist of a limited past life regression.

You do not need any previous experience with meditation or shamanic practice.
Simply come as you are.

-Shaman Phil

description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
How to Overcome Anger with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

Anger appears in many forms and disguises. Sometimes it manifests as a feeling of stress, other times it may take the form of depression. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. In this series we will explore practical solutions to the problem of anger, deconstructing its actual causes and learning viable alternatives to this painful habit of mind.

2nd and 4th Sundays

Now On-Line during Covid-19 Quarantine
10:00 a.m. – 12:15 p.m.
$0 - $25 (Included in our monthly pass)

Slow down and be with yourself through art making. A rich morning that feeds your spirit, rests your body, quiets your mind and helps you remember who you are!

Here we will use the arts to have a conversation with ourselves and connect to our longings and gifts. This is not about religion, yet in the inquiry you may choose to make connections to your religious beliefs.

The format: We check in as a group, we may do a little drumming, have 5 minutes of quiet/reflection/meditation/prayer/relaxation time, go create art in silence (without talking) doing our own thing and then come back together to honor what we spent our time doing.

Art making can be painting, writing, sand tray, collage, doodling, scribbling, sewing, mixed media, movement, or…. No previous art experience necessary just the willingness to follow what you are attracted to and moving slow and quiet.

title: Exhibition on Screen | The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Hieronymus Bosch – Visions of Genius at the Het Noordbrabants Museum (February 13–May 8, 2016) was the largest ever Bosch retrospective, bringing 36 of his 44 surviving works together in Den Bosch. The exhibition took a radical approach, offering research and conservation expertise in exchange for loans from the world’s best museums. Over 420,000 people flocked to the exhibition to marvel at Bosch’s curious creations, with opening hours extended to 1am to accommodate the phenomenal demand. 
Accompanied by expert insights from the exhibition’s curators and leading cultural critics, the film delves into the life of the visionary artist to explore the inspiration behind his strange and haunting works. Contributors include maverick filmmaker and artist Peter Greenaway, The Times’ Chief Art Critic Rachel Campbell-Johnston, and Director of the Het Noordbrabants Museum Dr. Charles de Mooij. 
The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch allows audiences to appreciate the detail of Bosch’s paintings like never before, offering close-up views of the curiosities hidden within his brimming canvases, from cannibalistic clergymen to three- headed birds.

title: New Moon Circle for All with Marian Noble
description:
Awakening Asheville
Join us for a welcoming and inclusive New Moon Circle, where all bodies and all genders are invited into sacred gathering. The New Moon is the seed point of the lunar cycle, a powerful time to pause, reflect, and plant clear intentions for the month ahead.

Our 90-minute circle opens with a grounding meditation to help you arrive fully in body and breath. We'll explore the astrological themes of this New Moon in an accessible way, then move into heart shares, holding space for one another in a supportive, non-judgmental circle. We'll close with a ritual aligned with this month's lunar energy to anchor your intentions.

You'll leave with greater clarity, deeper connection, and inspired momentum for the new lunar cycle. Whether you're new to moon rituals or a longtime practitioner, this circle offers insight, community, and renewal.

This month we gather under the Libra New Moon, an invitation to rebalance relationships, restore harmony, and call more beauty into everyday life.

Come as you are. Everyone is welcome. Bring your friends!

**Details**

* Sanctuary Studio, 81 Weaverville Rd., Suite 2, Woodfin, NC 28806
* Sunday, October 11 at 7 - 8:30 p.m.
* $22 per person. Space is intentionally limited to keep our circle intimate, so reserve your spot early.
* Please arrive a few minutes early to settle in.

**What to Bring**

* A journal and pen
* Any comfort items for your spot: blanket, pillow, bolster
* An altar item, such as a photo, a crystal, or something from nature, to help hold the imprint of our time together
* Your sober self. This is a substance-free gathering, so come as your own sacred being.
* Curiosity and an open mind and heart

**Our Circle Agreements**

* **All are welcome.** There is no competition or hierarchy here. No one is above or below another. We meet as equals, honoring the wisdom within each of us.
* **Self-awareness over judgment.** If judgment arises (because we are human), see it as an invitation to self-reflect. We are all mirrors for one another.
* **Confidentiality and respect.** This is a safe and sacred space. What is shared here stays here.
* **Honor your needs.** Move as you need to: get water, use the restroom, grab a tissue. You are a sovereign being and can care for yourself.
* **Emotions are sacred.** There's no need to hold back, apologize, or adjust your emotions to fit others. Your experience is your own medicine.
* **Witness, don't fix.** We honor each other as whole beings, holding space without assuming needs or rushing to console. Simply witnessing is enough.
* **Names and pronouns are honored.** Share yours if you wish. We commit to using them as an expression of care, presence, and mutual respect.

We will keep a moderate pace but take breaks for water and to look at the views. I will be watching the weather closely this weekend and will cancel if we get too much water. We should have some good fall colors although this year seems a bit muted.

https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/north-carolina/thompson-ridge-trail

The weather currently might be okay for Monday but I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:00 AM if there is a chance of severe weather or lightning during this time period..

location: Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St., Asheville, NC 28801
description:
Andy and Zack Page have been finishing each other's musical sentences since before either could drive. Born four minutes apart and raised in a house where blues records, old-time singing, and hard rock all shared the same air, the twins grew into a guitar and a bass that move like one nervous system, Andy's lines and Zack's low end tracking each other so closely the seam disappears. Under the Page Brothers name they lead a rotating cast through gypsy swing, straight-ahead jazz, fusion, and, when the mood turns, something closer to the metal they never quite outgrew. Tonight the cast runs four deep, and the two players rounding out the quartet have each spent a lifetime making music that record stores never knew where to shelve.

title: Autumn Plein Air Painting in the Gardens
description:
Autumn Plein Air Painting in the Gardens
with Erika Busse 
Tuesday, October 13  |  9 – 11 am 
Register Here!
There is no better way to relax and connect with your creative side and nature than en plein air painting. In this class, artist Erika Busse will teach you how to paint an original Appalachian inspired artwork outside at the beautiful North Carolina Arboretum. She will take you through each step of the painting process, all skill levels are welcomed and all supplies are provided. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Erika Busse moved to Asheville in 2017 after graduating from the University of Alabama with degrees in art and business. She is a small business owner of her full time artist business, sharing mountain inspired painting and printmaking with the world. She has been teaching plein air painting classes since 2021.

title: Buck Spring Trail; a Saunter
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
A seasonal favorite; this is a very pleasant hike that weaves in and out of the various coves that lie along the southeast face of the mountain ridge that rises up above Pink Beds. I suggest extra socks & towels for any surprises on the creek Xings.
We will be CATCHING Fall color.
I will be carrying the ‘Ent-Ward’ that gives us permission to pass thru the forest.
**DIFFICULTY:** rocky & dirt narrow trail. 6 moderately challenging rock-hop creek Xingsl. There may be unexpected challenges and obstacles.
**We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !!**
**John Muir didn’t like the word ‘hike’. *“We ought to saunter through them reverently, not 'hike' through them.”***
Details:
**(Social ‘hour’ at 9:45AM. Parade leaves at 9:55AM)**
Length: 4 mi (in & out) to Picnic Rock from Hwy 276 and back.
Accum ascent: 500 ft total (gradual). Pace: **1.5mph.**
**IF YOU HAVE AN ORANGE VEST; WEAR IT. HUNTING SEASON HAS STARTED. ;-) THEY ARE INEXPENSIVE AT WALMART....**
**Drive time: 20 min 1-way**
**Return Not earlier than: 2 pm (=4hrs)**
**Optional:** Late lunch after – at a location determined by the vimen….
Carpool contributions appreciated. $2.00 suggested
**THIS IS A DOG-PARTICIPANT HIKE.** This event is NOT for those who are uncomfortable with the antics of fun-loving dogs. Well trained dogs **(you don’t have to yell)** can be 'off-leash'. 'On leash' when meeting other hikers. Small (lap)dogs may carpool. Large dogs will drive themselves.
Incessant prattlers will be assumed to be having an affair.
Weather Check: Brevard, NC
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 1 driver(s)
We suggest open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others. Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.
Waiver: There are certain risks inherent in any outdoor activity. Each participant, by signing up to attend this event, agrees to release from liability the leader(s), Hendo Fun Friends, its Partners, Affiliates, and members for any accident, injury, illness, or personal loss which might occur while participating in this activity or while traveling in any vehicle during this trip. **Each participant further agrees to abide by the rules and regulations concerning safety, to follow instructions of the leader(s), and not to become intentionally separated from the group.** The leader(s) also has the right to use any images collected on this trip for recording on website photo collections.

Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! 
Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

title: Zorba the Greek - Kazantzakis
description:
Books That Age Like Wine
**First published in 1946, Zorba the Greek, is, on one hand, the story of a Greek working man named Zorba, a passionate lover of life, the unnamed narrator who he accompanies to Crete to work in a lignite mine, and the men and women of the town where they settle. On the other hand it is the story of God and man, The Devil and the Saints; the struggle of men to find their souls and purpose in life and it is about love, courage and faith.**

**Zorba has been acclaimed as one of the truly memorable creations of literature—a character created on a huge scale in the tradition of Falstaff and Sancho Panza. His years have not dimmed the gusto and amazement with which he responds to all life offers him, whether he is working in the mine, confronting mad monks in a mountain monastery, embellishing the tales of his life or making love to avoid sin. Zorba’s life is rich with all the joys and sorrows that living brings and his example awakens in the narrator an understanding of the true meaning of humanity. This is one of the greatest life-affirming novels of our time.**

**Part of the modern literary canon, Zorba the Greek, has achieved widespread international acclaim and recognition. This new edition translated, directly from Kazantzakis’s Greek original, is a more faithful rendition of his original language, ideas, and story, and presents Zorba as the author meant him to be.**

Rattlesnake Lodge to Folk Art Center along the MST  10 miles, 1400' elevation
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Meeting Spot**: Folk Art Center on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Prompt 8:00 departure
**Description**: This is a point to point hike. We will meet at the Folk Art Center and shuttle up to the Rattle Snake Lodge starting point. Follow the MST Trail from the remnants of the Rattlesnake Lodge, a turn of the century lodge built by an Asheville physician, to the Folk Art Center. There is a large variety of colorful wildflowers along the trail, which is mostly downhill with a few short climbs. There is a nice overlook for a lunch/snack break. Good footing. Shaded. Pace: 2.4 mph. Dogs welcome if on a leash. **Please Note:** This is a longer hike than my usual. If it's a warm day, I recommend bringing along extra water.

title: Let AI Work for You
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Let AI Work for You: Hand Your First Weekly Job to AI**

[Alan Nehemy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alannehemy/), founder of Metamorphosis Worldwide, shows how to hand a real weekly job to AI and let it do the work: a task that runs on a schedule, uses your own notes and files, and comes back to you for approval, instead of you having to remember to ask.
You'll see it built live, then pick one job from your own week to hand over.
Best for people who already use AI and want it to take work off their plate, not just answer questions. Bring a laptop with Claude or ChatGPT open.

**What to Bring**

1. A laptop (preferred) or tablet/smartphone.
2. An account created on ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.
3. Optional: A buddy or co-founder! (If you don't have a laptop, we will pair you up).

**Event Agenda**
5:30 PM – 6:00 PM: Networking, Drinks & Setup
6:00 PM – 7:30 PM: presentation

**Special discount on ADN engraved Pirani cups!**
Get $10 off our 5th anniversary customized [ADN Pirani cups](https://avldigitalnomads.org/meet-our-brand-new-customized-adn-pirani-mugs/)! Available in 16oz, 26oz, and 32oz sizes, you can select yours directly at this event.

**General Event Info**
AI Hacks and Hops is a monthly event tailored for non-technical professionals, entrepreneurs, marketers, engineers, or anyone who wants to explore and discuss how to use AI.

Each gathering will feature presentations, stimulating group discussions, and a relaxed atmosphere for enjoying your favorite brews while delving into the world of AI. Topics will range from AI integration in business processes, marketing, content creation, software, ethical considerations, human-AI collaboration strategies, to the latest advancements in AI technology. The informal setting encourages open dialogue, idea exchange, and fosters a collaborative spirit.

title: Shut Up & Write!® in Hendersonville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:** This event is moving to the Shut Up & Write! website. To RSVP to upcoming session or connect with other local writers, [join the new group page here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2x848mVGaJ ).

If you have any questions, feel free to [reach out here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/contact).

Thanks!
The Shut Up & Write! Team

\-\-\-

Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

When you show up, say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once you’re all settled, take some time to chat with your fellow writers. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

**A note about the format**
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://www.shutupwrite.com).

description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: "Lost Ground: America's Landslide Crisis" Film Screening
description:
UNC Asheville will be screening the recent documentary “Lost Ground: America’s Landslide Crisis” in Mullen & James Humanities Hall. The screening is to be followed by a panel discussion and Q&A moderated by the director, WCNC’s investigative reporter Nate Morabito.  
The panelists include:  

Paige Ambord and Caitlin Meagher, faculty in the Department of Sociology and Anthropology and who are featured in the film for their work on landslide survivors post-Helene
Jackie Langille, an expert on landslide geography in the Department of Environmental Science. 

This important film exposes the extent of landslide damage during Helene, and raises awareness of landslide risks, two years after that devastating event. 
 
Accessibility
UNC Asheville is committed to providing universal access to all of our events. If you have any questions about access or would like to request reasonable accommodations that will facilitate your full participation in the film screenings, please contact Stephanie Bullick, Director of Accessibility, at accessibility@unca.edu. 
Visitor Parking

All visitors must adhere to the University’s parking policy. Please visit the UNC Asheville Visitor Parking Permit Registration site to acquire a visitor permit to park on campus.

Rainbow Falls is one of the most spectacular waterfall settings in the Blue Ridge Mountains of North Carolina. This 150-ft. tall waterfall is impressive, especially after rainy weather that swells the Horsepasture River. The best feature of Rainbow Falls is the ability for visitors to experience the falls from the front, bottom, side and top! Rainbow Falls is just one of a series of cascades and waterfalls on a two-mile stretch of the river.
**Hidden, Turtleback & Drift Falls are included..**
https://www.romanticasheville.com/rainbow_falls.htm

We are the HFF Trail Trekkers: We a’gonna get our step-counters a’workin’ !! John Muir didn’t like the word ‘hike’. *“We ought to saunter through them reverently, not 'hike' through them.”*

title: Third Thursday | Educator's Night Out
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Every Third Thursday, the Museum comes alive with an evening filled with music, tours, art making, special cocktails in our rooftop café, and more! 
  
Educator’s Night Out: FREE admission for K–12 and college educators, administrators, and teaching artists (with valid ID) 
In addition to our regular Third Thursday programming, this month we invite K–12 and college educators, administrators, and teaching artists to join us for our Fall Educator’s Night Out. View the Museum’s current exhibitions, enjoy music, create art in the Studio, learn about our many tour offerings and opportunities to work with the Museum, and take time to socialize. Please preregister below.  
Schedule of Events  
5–5:30pm: Guided tour of The Art of Paper  
5:30–7pm: In this high energy ninety-minute workshop, Denise Markbreit, printmaker/educator & founder of printhouseavl.com will lead you through the steps necessary to create your own unique block print. You will come away with some newfound knowledge, skills, and a lovely collection of small prints to share with your students and friends. And it will be so much fun!!!  
Educator Preregistration 

  
Enjoy an evening of live music from 6–8pm performed by the Asheville Symphony Youth Orchestra’s talented chamber ensembles. Featuring a brass duo, three string quartets, and a clarinet duo, the two-hour program will bring energy, artistry, and inspiration to the Museum’s galleries.  

The Asheville Symphony Youth Orchestra program serves more than 200 of the very best young musicians in the greater Asheville area. The program consists of two string orchestras, two symphony orchestras, a percussion ensemble, a flute choir, a jazz combo, and numerous wind and string chamber ensembles. Students participate in masterclasses, retreats, workshops, tours and social events. They also receive high-quality music instruction from the region’s most respected professional conductors and musicians and have the opportunity to perform throughout the community. Most importantly, students involved in ASYO gain a strong sense of discipline, increased confidence, and a deep appreciation for music and the arts.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Rice Pinnacle Lollipop: 5.3 mi., 530 ft. Elev. Gain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**[Sign-up opens 8:00 PM, Sunday October 11th]**

**Please read the carpool info below the hike description.**

This is a typical lovely hike in the Bent Creek area. It incorporates segments from the Wolf Branch and Corvair Trails, along with several connectors. At 5.3 miles and a tame 530' elevation gain, I'd rate it 2.5 on a 0-10 difficulty scale. We'll average around 2.4 mph -- not a fitness hike, but you should have enough experience hiking to know you can deal with mild hills and a moderate pace.

We'll stop for a brief snack & water break halfway around. Wear sensible hiking boots. If you're on the fence about hiking poles, you probably don't need them for this one.

***Dog Policy:*** Dogs are extremely welcome but must be leashed.

***Guest Policy:*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they should join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own. Alternatively, contact me in advance and ask if it's okay to bring a "+1" after you've made it onto the "Going" list. Depending on timing and demand, I MAY be able to add your guest.

**MEET-UP TIME AND PLACE**
Optional carpooling on this hike, but it's encouraged. We'll rendezvous at the **Asheville Outlets parking lot, just behind the Waffle House on Brevard Rd. (Rt. 191)**. We'll leave there and head over to the Rice Pinnacle parking lot at **8:45 am**.

If you're parking at the trailhead, please come a few minutes early for check-in and intros. Look for me at my silver Hyundai. We'll hit the trail a.s.a.p. after 9:00 AM.

**DIRECTIONS TO TRAILHEAD**

* From Exit 33 on I-26,
* Head south on Brevard Rd. (Rt. 191) for 2 miles
* Right at the lights on Bent Creek Ranch Rd.
* After .3 miles bear left onto Wesley Branch Rd.
* Go about 1.4 miles and turn right just past the sign for the Rice Pinnacle Trailhead
* Go left at the fork. You'll see the parking lot after a short distance.

**Click here for the location on [Google Maps](https://maps.app.goo.gl/totfTN3YMWYcU9KE7)**

**COURTESY TO WAIT-LISTERS (Please abide!)**
Only sign up if you \*TRULY\* plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers will have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.

If you're on the waiting list, keep checking the evening before. Despite what I wrote above, we always get last-minute dropouts.

**WEATHER**
I'll monitor National Weather Service forecasts for the hike area and email cancellation messages by 7:30 AM if the forecast is for more than a 50% chance of precipitation.

**QUESTIONS?**
If you have any questions, message me through MeetUp until 8:30 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy, but you can try to text or call me up to the start of the hike: (803) 767-3094.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**LEGALESE**

This Asheville Hiking Group event involves hiking and, possibly, transportation to and from the meetup site. Participants are responsible for their own safety and, by joining a hike, affirm that they have the appropriate skills, physical conditioning, equipment, and supplies. Hiking may involve risks to oneself and property. Neither your hike organizer nor Asheville Hiking Group can eliminate all risks or be responsible for your well-being. Participants assume full responsibility for any injuries, damages, or losses.

title: LET THERE BE LIGHT!!: Mosaic Glass Block Lamp Workshop
description:
LET THERE BE LIGHT!!: Mosaic Glass Block Lamp Workshop
with Linda Pannullo 
Friday, October 16  |  10 – 4pm 
Register Here!
Bring some light into these short days!! Convert a 7″ Glass Block into a stunning mosaic table lamp. Great class for beginners – you will learn basic mosaic skills using glass nippers, running pliers and glass scorer. The afternoon will be spent covering both sides of the block. Grout if preferred, will be done at home and there will be a link to a grouting demo. Class comes with a complete kit that contains glass block, light for the inside, a rainbow array of cathedral glass cut into 3″ x 1″ pieces, handout, glue, paintbrush, popsicle sticks, grout, glass embellishments and extra glass for practice. All tools will be provided for the class. 
Linda Pannullo is a local mosaic artist that uses both traditional and contemporary for my art. Her work ranges from the whimsical to fine art, from eclectic materials to the traditional stained glass and 3D sculptures. She loves to teach and currently instructs at the John C Campbell Folk School in Brasstown, NC, Olive’s Porch, the Purple Crayon and Trackside Studios in Asheville. She is very fond of FUNctional Art and love bringing new folks into the mosaic world. One of her biggest honors is to be the 1st mosaic artist to exhibit at the NC Arboretum and have a permanent mosaic installation, Nature’s Throne there.

title: Fall Tree ID
description:
Fall Tree ID
With Lauren Lampley 
Friday, October 16  |  1pm – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
Join this class as we discuss how to use different characteristics and field guides to identify common trees of Western North Carolina found here at the NC Arboretum. We will look at using different characteristics including habitat, bark, buds, growth pattern, leaf shape, and fruit/nut shape to identify trees. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

title: History and Archaeology of the Arboretum
description:
History and Archaeology of the Arboretum
with Bob and Mary Noel 
Friday, October 16  |  1 – 4pm 
Register Here!
  
The land that makes up The North Carolina Arboretum has been home to different human groups over a span of more than 15,000 years. It has had many uses and been shaped by those who lived here. This walk, led by archaeologists Bob and Mary Noel, will give participants a chance to see and hear about past occupants of this land, and even a little history about how it became the state’s Arboretum. 
Bob and Mary Noel both had long careers as archaeologists with the US Forest Service. Bob worked mostly in North Carolina where he recorded thousands of sites on national forest lands here. Most of Mary’s archaeological work was in Idaho and Ohio. Both of them have been active in living history programs as well, most recently with the Heritage Alliance in Jonesborough, Tennessee. The Noels now have a consulting firm and still do archaeological survey projects. Mary can be found working at the Arboretum’s Baker Information desk several days a week, sharing her knowledge of local trails, gardens and history.

Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Hope - Ecstatic Dance Wave w/ Sara Bensman
description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Friday, October 16th
Evening Dance Wave 7:00 pm \- 9:00 pm \| Warmup 7pm \| Opening Circle 7:30pm
Facilitator Sara Bensman

Intention: Hope

In times of change that are unprecedented, anxiety-producing and far reaching, it feels helpful to explore the edges and embodied experience of the verb Hope.

Hope Is Not a Bird, Emily, It’s a Sewer Rat
*by Caitlin Seida*

Hope is not the thing with feathers
That comes home to roost
When you need it most.
Hope is an ugly thing
With teeth and claws and
Patchy fur that’s seen some shit.
It’s what thrives in the discards
And survives in the ugliest parts of our world,
Able to find a way to go on
When nothing else can even find a way in.
It’s the gritty, nasty little carrier of such
diseases as
optimism, persistence,
Perseverance and joy,
Transmissible as it drags its tail across
your path
and
bites you in the ass.
Hope is not some delicate, beautiful bird,
Emily.
It’s a lowly little sewer rat
That snorts pesticides like they were
Lines of coke and still
Shows up on time to work the next day
Looking no worse for wear.

title: Queen Bee and the Honeylovers
location: Meadow at Highland Brewing Co., 12 Old Charlotte Highway, Suite 200, Asheville, NC, 28803, United States
description:
Sweet, sweet Swing










Queen Bee and the Honeylovers are rooted in the jazz and blues of the 1930’s and 40’s. Their original compositions nod to these classic styles with lyrical content that explores modern themes that feel both timeless and immediate.  Their debut album, ‘Asheville’, celebrated their hometown’s history and won them #41 on WNCW’s listener-voted poll of Best Albums of 2019 as well as features on The State of Things with Frank Stasio and PBS Woodsongs. Their video for “Beacham’s Curve” won Best Soundtrack at the 2019 Music Video Asheville Awards. The Honeylovers approach early jazz not as a static genre but as a living language. Their work reflects an ongoing dialogue between past and present, using the forms of early American music to explore contemporary questions of place, identity, and cultural memory. The result is a sound that is both historically informed and distinctly of the moment, delivering equal parts vintage swing, original storytelling, and high-energy connection with the audience. 
Weekend Live Music
Highland Brewing’s weekend live music series showcases incredible local talent, regional acts and national touring bands from across the East Coast and beyond. Free and open to all ages (unless noted otherwise), it’s the perfect excuse to gather your crew, listen and vibe to a wide range of genres including soul, bluegrass, acoustic, country, folk and more.
Live music typically takes place on our scenic Meadow stage. Shows are rain or shine, if the weather doesn’t cooperate and we have time to move inside, the band will play in the Taproom where there’s still plenty of room to boogie.
Chairs, blankets and well-behaved, leashed pets are welcome in the Meadow. Please note that coolers and outside alcohol are not permitted on the premises.

April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Let's Walk: It's Leaf Season at the NC Arboretum
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet inside the Baker Visitor Center. Restrooms are available at the start point. We will start walking as soon as everyone has arrived.

The walk is a guided 5 KM trail. There are some moderate hills and stair climbing. A significant part of the route is on well-groomed trails with very few obstacles. Some people will want walking poles.

We will walk down Wesley Branch Trail to Bent Creek Road. Traveling down Bent Creek Road, we will loop through the Azalea Garden a little further than we usually go. The Azaleas won't be in bloom, but it will be leaf season after all. We will continue down Bent Creek Road, returning to the parking lot via Wolf Branch Road and Greenhouse Way. Before we quit, we will walk through the Bonsai Exhibition Garden and the Formal Gardens.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome but are not allowed in buildings or in the Bonsai Exhibit. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $25 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend the driver purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher-level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year.

title: Downtown Asheville Scavenger Hunt 3.0
description:
Friendly People in Asheville
Hi everyone! It's time for our Fall Downtown Asheville Scavenger Hunt 3.0!

Brand new clues and extra bonus questions this time! Whether you're new to the area or know downtown well, this is a fun way to explore Asheville and make new friends.

**Here's how it works:**
We will gather at Bear's Smokehouse at 135 Coxe Avenue at 2:30pm. We’ll hang out for a bit -- plenty of time for a drink or a snack.
We will break into teams and go over the rules at 3:15pm. Teams will have 10-15 minutes to review the clues, and the hunt will begin at 3:30pm.

Teams will have an hour to hunt for 40 clues scattered across downtown and take a selfie with each clue. \*Bonus points for taking a selfie with the clue and a willing stranger. More willing strangers = more points.\*

The hunt ends at 4:30pm back at Bear's.
It will take 20-30 minutes to review all the teams’ answers and determine the winner.
The prize will be the glory of winning! 🏆

**What to bring:**

* Walking or running shoes (the hunt spans from South Slope to the north end of downtown)
* Your phone for taking pics
* A pencil or pen to mark off clues as you find them
* Your competitive spirit!

**Parking:**
Parking is available nearby at the Coxe Ave Garage (52 Coxe Ave). Metered street parking is also available on various side streets.

**Disclaimer and Release of Liability:**
Participants are responsible for their safety. If you sign up or participate in this event, you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event.

Looking forward to seeing y’all there!

title: The Tao of Unknotting - Ecstatic Dance Waves w/ Conway Weary
description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Sunday, October 18th
1st Dance Wave 8:30\-10:30am \| Warmup 8:30am \| Opening Circle 9am
2nd Dance Wave 10:30\-12:30am \| Warmup 10:30am \| Opening Circle 11am
Auxiliary Facilitator Conway Weary

Intention: The Tao of Unknotting
A blessing on the knots that were tied into you, and that you learnt to tie into yourself, until you were woven into a net that could catch approval and diplomas and lovers.

A blessing on your toil that yielded worldly riches when you were cast into the great ocean of suffering and returned laden with jewels and trinkets and heartbreak.

A blessing on the seaweed that clogged your mesh and dragged you down and snagged you on rocks and anchors.

A blessing on the tide that stranded you on this shore, discarding you like debris, rendering your knotted self useless.

A blessing on the knots that were tied into you, and that you tied into yourself. May each one loosen now. Though it once held you together and made you strong, it binds you where you no longer need to be bound.

Something greater holds you now. May this knot loosen, and this, and this.

A blessing on your unravelling that feels a little like insanity. You're not going mad. May the sun warm the places that were tied so tight it felt like suffocating. And now that it is safe, to soften, to loosen, to breathe, fill your lungs with the oxygen of freedom. Exhale. May your soul be released from the bondage of survival, and unlaced, relax into unboundedness. And bask in the blessing of letting go.

By Shao Lan

## About Conway Weary

Conway remembers the moment. Her first grade teacher, Mrs. Dean, lined up the girls, put Tchaikovsky on the record player and said, "Pretend you are a flower". That ecstatic meeting of music, movement and imagination was a moment that set a life direction. The Dancer's Path is where the outside meets the inside, the healer meets the wound, and body and soul play passionately with the edges of life. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. David Alvarado, a Chicano documentary filmmaker, is passionate about science, technology, and human rights. title: Sunday Walk at Little Champion Plant in Waynesville
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Old Timers call this property on Old Howell Mill Road near Old Asheville Highway "Little Champion" because the Canton Champion Paper Mill put in this plant to put wax on paper for making milk cartons. The Mill changed hands several times, but the Old Timers kept calling it Little Champion. (Note that Google Maps calls it Evergreen Packaging, and the sign on the building now says Suzano.)

The 3/4-mile walking track at Little Champion runs by Richland Creek with lots of creekside trees, by fishing spots, and by a picnic area. There is a bathroom in the middle of the track. We plan to do 4 clockwise laps. (Yes, you are free to do fewer or even more!) That will make a total of 5 KM/3.1 miles.

Be sure you enter the property on the Old Asheville Highway (east) side of the plant (the side with the Suzano sign) on Ken Thompson Drive, go to the rear of the building, and then turning left, go ***all the way to the far end of the back of the parking lot, down by the sign designating the Drop Lot***. It is in that corner of the parking lot where we will assemble. (If you go down the stairs into the middle of the track, you will be in the wrong place and will miss where the group is assembling.)

Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. There is a little hill on each lap, so some may want walking sticks (I plan to use 1 stick). Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. This is a paved track, so tennis shoes will be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers will have no problem.

title: Free Cuddle @ the Park/Show; Hope of OZ
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
this is a free event but **[please register HERE](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/free-cuddle-the-parkshow-montfort-players-hope-of-oz)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/free-cuddle-the-parkshow-montfort-players-hope-of-oz)so we have a final head count.

Come cuddle in the park while watching local free (donations encouraged) theater! The **Montford Players** are preforming **Hope of OZ** and you are invited to come watch the show with the Asheville Cuddle Collective. Note- we will not be doing icebreakers or connection games. You are welcome to ask people to cuddle or share touch and as always, wait for an enthusiastic yes before touching anyone.

Show begins at 7:30- we will gather our blankets and start connecting at 7pm.
[https://www.exploreasheville.com/asheville/events/hope-oz](https://www.exploreasheville.com/asheville/events/hope-oz)

What to bring- Please bring a blanket and pillow to help create the cuddle space. Bring your own water & snacks to share.
You are welcome to bring friends. Children are welcome at this event!

**Reminder - Touch is always optional** at these events**.** Come as you are, wear comfy clothes, and let your nervous system breathe in the fresh air.

finding us- Park in the parking lot and walk down the hill to the amphitheater. We will try to find a space in the 2nd or 3rd row.

Set a decade after Dorothy’s defeat of the Wicked Witch of the West and her subsequent departure, The Hope of Oz brings us to a newly invigorated Capital where the Wizard’s power has grown immensely with constant systematic oppression on his denizens and waging a drug-fueled war with the new cadre of Witches that brings its citizens to their knees. The story follows Gale, an investigative “Witch-hunter,” on the trail of East’s assassination. Trapped in a bar with a synthetic (known as mimics), surrounded by encroaching revolutionaries, Witches, and the Wizard’s ever watchful eyes, Gale must survive the night if Oz will see its dawn. But in an empire of extremes, who can survive?

If there is heavy RAIN - We will cancel this event.

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

description:
oin students and faculty to learn about Inside-Out, the College’s higher education in prison program in partnership with Western Correctional Center for Women. Inside-Out is the only program in North Carolina that brings together college students (“Outside”) with incarcerated students (“Inside”) for credit‑bearing courses taught inside the prison.

At this information session, you’ll hear about the courses being offered in Spring Semester 2027, learn how the program works, and listen to first‑hand experiences from students who have participated in Inside-Out classrooms. You’ll also have a chance to ask questions and explore how Inside-Out connects to social justice learning, community engagement, and equity through higher education in prison.

title: Ribbon cutting for the Broadway Public Safety Station Public Art project
Bonsai Exhibit Talk and Tour with Arthur Joura
description:
Bonsai Exhibit Talk and Tour with Arthur Joura
Tuesday, October 20  |  5:30 – 7pm 
Register Here!
Join Bonsai Curator Arthur Joura on this entertaining and informative after-hours tour of the garden at its peak in autumn, a fitting showcase for the specimens and the miniature landscapes. As Joura says, “The two things are one: The garden is designed to elevate the experience of bonsai, and the bonsai never look better than when they’re on display in the garden.” 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Arthur Joura has been the bonsai curator at the Arboretum since 1992 and oversaw the design and development of the Arboretum’s Bonsai Exhibition Garden. Joura augmented early training in fine art and studied bonsai with some of the leading bonsai authorities in the United States and in Japan. His greatest teachers are trees, however. His love of hiking and photographing trees in nature has shaped the Arboretum’s collection and firmly rooted it in a regional identify — one that elevates naturalism in art and the use of traditional bonsai species alongside species native to the Southern Appalachian mountains — creating in the process one of the most acclaimed public collections of bonsai in the country.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: Sapphic Book Club!  - September
description:
Queers to the Front!
Our book club read for October is *Pumpkin Spice and Poltergeist* by Ali K. Mulford and K. Elle Morrison

**Get ready for a bewitching tale of love, laughter, and supernatural shenanigans in the heart of Maple Hollow!**

The last thing apothecary witch, Jordyn, had on her mind was romance, but when she got witchy-wasted, she cracked open the coffin of her love life and conjured the ghost of her ex-girlfriend.

Jordyn is in for a spell of trouble now that the snarky specter is determined to haunt her until she finds someone new.

Enter Harlow, the new girl in town, who just wants a job in her sister's cafe but she discovers that the spooky town of Maple Hollow is more than just a gimmick. Real magic lives here. But after run-ins with vampires and one too many grave cafe blunders, she's ready to hop on a broomstick and fly out of town. Until she finds herself falling under the spell of the enchanting witch who asks her on a date.

As sparks fly and cauldrons bubble, will this unlikely pair brew up a love potion that defies the ghostly odds? Or will Jordyn's shade-y ex be the ultimate buzzkill to their budding romance?

Grab your broomstick and buckle up for a cozy sapphic paranormal rom-com that's sure to cast a spell on your heart this fall season!

title: Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall
location: Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St., Asheville, NC 28801
description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.

Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...
