title: Introduction to Appalachian Ecology
description:
Introduction to Appalachian Ecology
with Dan Lazar 
Wedesday, October 21  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Core 
Register Here!
From the flood plain of the French Broad River to the summit of Mount Mitchel, we will explore the diverse ecological communities that make up the Blue Ridge Bioregion. We will learn why spruce trees are found only on the summits of our highest mountains: why the Southern Appalachians are the lungless salamander capital of the world; and how deer and ants determine where trilliums grow. Part illustrated lecture and part on-site field trip, this class serves as an introduction to all Special Topics in Ecology classes offered through the Blue Ridge Naturalist Program. 
This program takes place in the classroom and outdoors. Please come prepared to walk on gentle, yet uneven terrain, and dress appropriately for the weather. 
 Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

title: 🌄 Remembering Together: The Power of Spiritual Community
description:
Center for Spiritual Living Asheville
# 🌄 Remembering Together: The Power of Spiritual Community

✨ **An Interactive Workshop with Forrest Rivers** ✨

📅 **Wednesday, October 21st**
🕡 **6:30 PM**
📍 **Center for Spiritual Living Asheville**
2 Science of Mind Way, Asheville, NC 28806

What is the power of coming together in spiritual community? ❤️
It has been called by many names: *Sangha, Church, Satsang,* and spiritual community. Whatever name we use to describe this sacred gathering of souls, one thing is certain: coming together in spiritual community can be a powerful and transcendent experience.

Join workshop facilitator **Forrest Rivers** for an engaging, highly interactive exploration of why we are drawn to gather with fellow spiritual seekers and how these connections can deepen our relationship with the living spirit.

🌿 **Together, we'll explore questions such as:**
✨ Why are we drawn as spiritual seekers to gather in the spirit?
🙏 How does meeting in Sangha (spiritual community) draw us closer to a deeper relationship with the living spirit?
💜 How do we find a spiritual community that truly resonates with our own unique journey?

Through heartfelt discussion, group chanting and sacred music, and contemplative exercises, we'll explore these questions together and discover the transformative possibilities of spiritual connection.

As Ram Dass so beautifully expressed, the true power of spiritual community lies in remembering that:

💜 *“We are all just walking each other home.”*

Come share in an evening of connection, reflection, music, and spiritual discovery. Whether you're already part of a spiritual community or seeking a place where you feel a deeper sense of belonging, you're invited to join us!

🌟 **We look forward to remembering together!**

#RememberingTogether #SpiritualCommunity #Sangha #SpiritualGrowth #HeartfeltConnection #ConsciousLiving #CenterForSpiritualLivingAsheville #CommunityCommonsAsheville

title: Hidden in Plain Sight
description:
Hidden in Plain Sight
with Eric Young 
Thursday, October 22 |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Wildlife plays tricks on each other to survive.  Predators blend-in to surprise prey.  The prey blends in to hide from predators. Not only will participants discover some of the best camouflaged animals in nature but they will also have their observation skills tested. There are many ways that nature hides wildlife, join naturalist/environmental educator, Eric Young, and come find out the many adaptations wildlife employs to stay alive. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Eric Young retired down to North Carolina in 2020 after 23 years as a program director at the nature center on Long island. He has dedicated  his life to the field of environmental education over his 35 years. title: Manifesting Self
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**Location Change:**
**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

Manifesting Self may sound a little out there. Trust me. It’s not. Whether we’ve been in the remote space for years, since the pandemic, or just recently, I’m certain it has changed each of us in ways we never thought possible. Let’s explore that together. The highs, the lows, and everywhere in between. And from there experience growth.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

title: The Stranger Hour: A Non-Networking Experiment
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
Confession time: we love our people. Maybe a little too much. At every social, we see the same happy circles, and we get it. Your friends are great. But somewhere out there tonight is your next great friend, and you haven't met them yet.

So here's the challenge.

**The Rules**

1. From 6:00 to 7:30, you can't talk to anyone you knew before tonight.
2. Waves are free. Conversations are not.
3. Came with a friend? Split up at 6:00 sharp.

**The Stakes:** If you're caught chatting with someone you already know, you both owe a beverage (booze optional) to whoever called you out. Yes, your friends will absolutely be watching you.

**The Reunion:** At 7:30, find your crew and bring at least one new friend with you.

New to ADN? Congratulations, you already know the rules better than anyone. Everyone here is a stranger to someone tonight.

The game starts at 6:00 on the dot, so come on time. Will you accept the challenge?

title: BLUEGRASS JAM SPECIAL EDITION FEATURING THE DARREN NICHOLSON BAND
description:
A Grammy nominee and the winner of 13 International Bluegrass Music Association awards, Darren Nicholson has taken his own brand of mountain music around the world. A regular for years on the Grand Ole Opry and a founding member of acclaimed bluegrass group Balsam Range, Darren now spends his time recording, writing new songs, and performing original roots music inspired by the history & culture of his native Western North Carolina — homegrown, wholehearted music with a purpose.



A punchy mandolinist with instrumentation nods to Bill Monroe and Marty Stuart, Darren is also an introspective songwriter, technical harmony singer, convincing lead vocalist, and a man on a mission. His shows are a tailored experience — genuine, entertaining, and an extended handshake to the community, reflecting the fun-witted and approachable character formed in his raising.



Darren’s passion is sharing raw, honest-to-goodness, quality music with his audience. Music that’s good for his soul and theirs too. “That’s all I want,” says Darren. “I want to be a positive part of other people’s lives with music, you know? I want to be an ambassador to roots music – tip my hat to the past while looking forward at the same time. This music was intended to be played in a way that adds joy to the community. All I want is to restore that purpose, not to complete a transaction.” 



Darren says that when you come out to a show, whatever you do, please come talk afterward. “I’m like Willie Nelson. ‘I don’t want fans, I want friends.’ It’s a communal thing.” 



Joining Darren on vocals are seasoned full-time band member AVERY WELTER (guitar) along with Avery’s former Shedhouse Trio partners SARAH GRIFFIN (upright bass) and BRADY WALLEN (banjo), both of whom are now full-time members of The Darren Nicholson Band as well.



This expanded full-time lineup brings together a powerhouse of Appalachian musicians with deep roots in traditional bluegrass and a shared passion for music, reflecting Darren’s continuing commitment to evolving his approach to bluegrass.



“I couldn’t be more thrilled . . . this means new sounds and new material. I can’t wait to see what this new chapter holds. And I think folks who come out to see the new band will be as blown away by their music as I am.”



This newest iteration of the band is rooted in the sounds of the Appalachian mountains yet unafraid to explore new territory — with strong instrumental interplay, distinctive vocal harmonies, original material, and the energy of four musicians who are deeply connected to the music.



Doors at 6pm — show starts at 7pm. Suggested cover at the door. Open Jam follows at 9:30pm.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Nielsen Big Idea Lecture: What Does Homophobia Have to Do With Racism?
location: Canon Lounge in Gladfelter Student Center
description:
Join Warren Wilson College for a Nielsen Big Idea Lecture featuring Ladelle McWhorter, Chair of Gender & Sexuality Studies at the University of Richmond.
 

In her talk, “What Does Homophobia Have to Do With Racism? Let’s Look at the History,” McWhorter will explore the historical connections between homophobia, racism, and systems of oppression. Drawing from her scholarship and decades of work in social justice, she will examine how these histories intersect and continue to shape our communities today.
 

McWhorter is the author of Bodies and Pleasures, Racism and Sexual Oppression in Anglo-America and Unbecoming Persons. She has worked for social justice for more than thirty years with Virginia Organizing, a grassroots organization dedicated to dismantling racism, fighting poverty and environmental injustice, and training ordinary Virginians to advocate for themselves and their communities.

title: River Systems Field Class
description:
River Systems Field Class
with Anton DuMars 
Friday, October 23  |  11am – 5pm 
BRN – Core 
Register Here!
For the River Systems Field Experience, we will observe processes and indicators along the Davidson River, a Blue Ridge tributary of the French Broad catchment basin. We consider channel hierarchy (first order, second order, etc.). Our stops include observation and discussions of flow and flood indicators and river forms, such as cut banks, point bars, and flood channels. We observe sediment texture, sediment load, and consider sediment source. 
 This program provides transportation to and from the class location using our minibus. We will meet at the Arboretum and return to the Arboretum. If you prefer to meet us there, let us know and we will tell you where to meet.  
This program will take place outside and will follow easy to moderate trails. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Anton DuMars, a resident of Black Mountain, NC, is an adjunct professor at the College of Charleston. His geological interests include fluvial, deltaic, and coastal processes. Ideally, he’s spending time on a hiking trail or aboard his sailboat.

Planning a great rose garden doesn’t begin in spring, the work begins with thoughtful planning through the quiet days of winter. Every hour spent preparing now is rewarded with healthier plants and more time to enjoy your garden in the spring. During this class learn best practices, tips and tricks, and other work that goes into planning and maintaining a great rose garden. This class is part of a series of offerings in collaboration with the Asheville Blue Ridge Rose Society as part of their Rose Grower’s School. 
John Smith is a Past President of Asheville- Blue Ridge Rose Society and is a Certified Consulting Rosarian for the American Rose Society since 2010. He has been growing roses since 1979 in New Jersey, California and now in North Carolina. For the past 8 years, John has been the manager of the Asheville Blue Ridge Rose Society’s test garden and for 16 years has been a Rosarian Assistant for the Biltmore Rose Garden.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
**[REGISTER HERE](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/oct-23rd-queer-platonic-cuddle)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/oct-23rd-queer-platonic-cuddle)(rsvp's on Meetup do not count as registering)
This is an event for Adults who identify as LGBTQIA+.
The intention of this event is to build community and provide a supportive place for participants to explore sweet platonic physical touch.
No one turned away for lack of funds (please ask if you truly need a scholarship or work trade).
**This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch.** We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

Consent and respect are at the forefront of the experience. We strive for a safe and welcoming environment, fostering a sense of trust that allows attendees to fully enjoy shared touch without any pressure or expectations.

Discover the joy of shared vulnerability in an environment where your authenticity is not just accepted but celebrated. This event is an opportunity to connect with like-minded individuals who appreciate the simplicity of human touch and the profound impact it can have on our well-being.

Express yourself in a way that feels true to you, whether through cozy attire or a touch of personal flair. We encourage individuality and self-expression, creating an inclusive space where everyone can be their authentic selves. Dress code is Casual and cozy.

This is an inclusive environment where we will aim to foster the dismantling of and no tolerance of ableism, fat-shaming, homophobia/transphobia, sexism, xenophobia, classism, racism & other ideas that lead to folks feeling disconnected or unwelcome.

**THE RULES**
1\. Pants stay on for the whole event\.
2\. You do not have to touch anyone at this event\.
3\. You must ask permission and receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone\. Please be specific in your requests\.
4\. If you feel a yes\, say YES\. If you feel a no\, say NO\. If you’re a maybe\, say NO\. You can always change your mind\.
5\. Get your facilitator if you have a question or concern\, or if you need assistance with anything during the event\.
6\. Talking\, laughter\, silence\, silliness\, stillness\, and crying are welcome\.

**ETIQUETTE**

* ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle.
* Please be free of strong scents; many folks would rather not be close to someone who smells of perfume, essential oils, or cigarettes
* BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share. The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

We take individual and group safety seriously! if you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at a touch based event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy- Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid. Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event. No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: Adult Studio: Introduction to Papermaking
location: NC
description:
This workshop will give you hands-on experience working with several pulps to learn the basics of Western style mould and deckle papermaking. 
Join us to learn: 

how to process recycled and commercial fibers into pulp at home or in a paper studio.
what tools and equipment are needed for papermaking.
how to pull, press and dry sheets of paper.

The day will start with a discussion about papermaking and will explore a variety of handmade paper samples. Afterwards, we will set up vats of pulp and make sheets of paper together. Each participant will take home a stack of sample papers. It’s up to you how you use the finished sheets. All are welcome. No experience necessary. 
ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST
Alyssa Sacora (she/her) is a crafts person working in plant-based mediums of papermaking, book arts, basketry, and weaving. She finds inspiration by observing relationships between plants and humans throughout time. To reduce her footprint and encourage creative thinking, she primarily works with locally available and repurposed natural materials. In addition to and in support of her craft, she tends a large garden in Fairview, North Carolina with fruits and vegetables, medicinal herbs, and art plants. 
Alyssa has taught for a variety of organizations in Western North Carolina and often utilizes an outside setting to help her students make the connection that we are nature and that our lives are intertwined with the plants, the soil, and the air around us. To learn more about Alyssa, see her work and course offerings, visit www.thepatchworkunderground.com.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: How to Overcome Anger
description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
How to Overcome Anger with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

Anger appears in many forms and disguises. Sometimes it manifests as a feeling of stress, other times it may take the form of depression. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. In this series we will explore practical solutions to the problem of anger, deconstructing its actual causes and learning viable alternatives to this painful habit of mind.

title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

Venue Guidelines: Please thank our hosts by purchasing something.

title: Exhibition on Screen | The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Hieronymus Bosch – Visions of Genius at the Het Noordbrabants Museum (February 13–May 8, 2016) was the largest ever Bosch retrospective, bringing 36 of his 44 surviving works together in Den Bosch. The exhibition took a radical approach, offering research and conservation expertise in exchange for loans from the world’s best museums. Over 420,000 people flocked to the exhibition to marvel at Bosch’s curious creations, with opening hours extended to 1am to accommodate the phenomenal demand. 
Accompanied by expert insights from the exhibition’s curators and leading cultural critics, the film delves into the life of the visionary artist to explore the inspiration behind his strange and haunting works. Contributors include maverick filmmaker and artist Peter Greenaway, The Times’ Chief Art Critic Rachel Campbell-Johnston, and Director of the Het Noordbrabants Museum Dr. Charles de Mooij. 
The Curious World of Hieronymus Bosch allows audiences to appreciate the detail of Bosch’s paintings like never before, offering close-up views of the curiosities hidden within his brimming canvases, from cannibalistic clergymen to three- headed birds. 
Purchase Tickets

title: Jazz, Gin, Money & Murder: Murder Mystery Party
description:
It’s 1923, and the party’s roarin’ — until an unwelcomed guest is found dead. Think you’ve got the detective skills to find out whodunnit?
Is the murderer a flapping dancer, a jazzy musician or a slyly deferential server? Maybe it will be—YOU! 
The Mule invites you for an immersive evening of delicious drinks, snazzy outfits, and big mystery – all set to the sounds of a live jazz band! 
The two-hour game rules are simple: arrive in character, follow the detective’s instructions, read from your script and sleuth out the murderer. You may even make some new friends, or enemies, along the way. 
This time, we’re giving everyone a chance to enjoy the party. Love dressing up, trying on a sharp Transatlantic accent, and putting on a show? You’ll want to PLAY! Love a good murder mystery and a reason to get snazzy, but public speaking doesn’t really jive with you? Join us as a spectator! 
PLAYERS: 

You ARE the show. Once you receive your character packet, it’s important that you commit to their voice, demeanor and aesthetic. This is a chance to let your creativity shine.
You will be required to converse with strangers and deliver your script through a microphone.
We kindly ask that only those who truly want the part choose to play.
We will send you your character packets by mail. Please do NOT share the contents of your packet with others in your party, as YOU could be the murderer!

SPECTATORS: 

You’ll have the opportunity to be in on the fun without taking center stage. Your excitement and energy is essential to filling the room.
We strongly encourage all our guests to come in costume, so throw together your best 20’s getup!
Be prepared to gasp, clap, laugh & certainly be entertained!

Both Players and Spectators will take a swing at finding the killer! The winning Player will win a grand prize, while all Spectators who guess correctly will receive a small participation token. Music, welcome drinks and hors d’oeuvres are offered for all in attendance to enjoy. 
Seats are limited so don’t delay! Player ticket sales end on October 14th. 
 Get Your Tickets!

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. title: Backyard Baskets: Coiling with Natural Materials
description:
Backyard Baskets: Coiling with Natural Materials
with Alyssa Sacora 
Wednesday, October 28 |  10 – 4pm 
Register Here!
Many local plants lend themselves to basket making. In this workshop, we will create a coiled vessel using leaves and grasses harvested from cultivated gardens and wild places. Coiling is a hand-stitching process that transforms a continuous bundle of fibers into a strong and versatile container. Found in cultures worldwide, it is a beautiful technique to create one-of-a-kind baskets from plants growing in your backyard. 
Participants can choose to complete a small basket in class or leave with extra materials to continue their basket at home. Coiling is great for beginner basket makers and those with weaving experience that want to learn more about using local plants in their creative practice. Please note that coiling requires adequate hand strength and decent eyesight. Accommodations will be made as best as possible to support participants who may have physical limitations. All materials are provided for this workshop. 
 Alyssa Sacora is a crafts person exploring plant-based mediums in the form of papermaking, book arts, basketry and natural dyes. She finds inspiration by observing relationships in the wider world. To reduce her human footprint and encourage creative thinking, she primarily works with locally available and repurposed natural materials. Leaves, vines and bark from iris, daylily, kudzu, okra, tulip poplar and willow leaves are often combined with salvaged cotton fabrics to create her palette. Her artistic pursuits are directly related to her lifestyle choices with reciprocity and mindfulness as a guiding force. In addition to and in support of her craft, she tends a 3-acre homestead in Western North Carolina with her husband, Adam. They grow fruits and vegetables, medicinal herbs, and art plants. They use solar electric and solar thermal systems for electricity and heating, collect rain water and continuously look to design their space with sustainability in mind. Alyssa has taught for a variety of organizations in WNC and often utilizes an outside setting to help her students make the connection that we are nature and that our lives are intertwined with the plants, the soil, and the air around us.

description:
It’s 1923, and the party’s roarin’ — until an unwelcomed guest is found dead. Think you’ve got the detective skills to find out whodunnit?
Is the murderer a flapping dancer, a jazzy musician or a slyly deferential server? Maybe it will be—YOU! 
The Mule invites you for an immersive evening of delicious drinks, snazzy outfits, and big mystery – all set to the sounds of a live jazz band! 
The two-hour game rules are simple: arrive in character, follow the detective’s instructions, read from your script and sleuth out the murderer. You may even make some new friends, or enemies, along the way. 
This time, we’re giving everyone a chance to enjoy the party. Love dressing up, trying on a sharp Transatlantic accent, and putting on a show? You’ll want to PLAY! Love a good murder mystery and a reason to get snazzy, but public speaking doesn’t really jive with you? Join us as a spectator! 
PLAYERS: 

You ARE the show. Once you receive your character packet, it’s important that you commit to their voice, demeanor and aesthetic. This is a chance to let your creativity shine.
You will be required to converse with strangers and deliver your script through a microphone.
We kindly ask that only those who truly want the part choose to play.
We will send you your character packets by mail. Please do NOT share the contents of your packet with others in your party, as YOU could be the murderer!

SPECTATORS: 

You’ll have the opportunity to be in on the fun without taking center stage. Your excitement and energy is essential to filling the room.
We strongly encourage all our guests to come in costume, so throw together your best 20’s getup!
Be prepared to gasp, clap, laugh & certainly be entertained!

Both Players and Spectators will take a swing at finding the killer! The winning Player will win a grand prize, while all Spectators who guess correctly will receive a small participation token. Music, welcome drinks and hors d’oeuvres are offered for all in attendance to enjoy. 
Seats are limited so don’t delay! Player ticket sales end on October 14th.

title: How Plants Respond to Their Environment
description:
How Plants Respond to Their Environment
with Alexandra Holland 
Thursday, October 29  |  1 – 2:30pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
How do plants handle stress?  How do they respond to their environment?  In this class we’ll explore plant hormones and movements, as well as how plants respond to stressful conditions such as droughts and extreme temperatures.  Prerequisite:  Beginning 
Alexandra Holland has a passion for getting people excited about the natural world through classes, hikes, and photography.  She graduated from Duke University and earned her master’s degree in botany from the University of Texas at Austin.  While in Texas, Alexandra managed the UTEX Culture Collection of Algae at UT Austin and volunteered with education programs at the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center.  Upon moving to Asheville, she began volunteering with the NC Arboretum’s youth education programs.  In 2008 she was in the first class of students to be certified as Blue Ridge Naturalists.   Alexandra teaches botany classes at the NC Arboretum and leads nature hikes in Western NC for groups of all ages.

title: Classy Cocktails at Capella on 9
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
Classy Cocktails: Nine Floors Up 🍸✨

Okay, Classy Cocktailers, we’re taking the word classy rather seriously this month.

For October, we’re heading nine floors above downtown Asheville to Capella on 9, the gorgeous rooftop bar at the AC Hotel, for cocktails, conversation and one seriously good view.

And yes, it is every bit as fabulous as it looks.

Wednesday, October 29

6:30 to 8:30 PM

Capella on 9

10 Broadway, 9th Floor, Downtown Asheville

Capella is one of those places that makes you want to sit down, order something pretty in a glass and stay awhile.

The rooftop overlooks downtown and the Blue Ridge Mountains, with fire features, sophisticated lounge spaces and that magical Asheville-at-dusk backdrop that should be showing off nicely right around the time we arrive. Inside, the space is sleek, modern and seriously elevated. Literally and otherwise. 😏

The cocktail menu goes well beyond your basic gin and tonic, with house-crafted drinks, barrel-select cocktails and creations like their Smoked Bourbon Old Fashioned. If cocktails aren’t your thing, there’s wine, bubbles, local beer and non-alcoholic options too.

And nobody needs to drink dinner. Capella also serves tapas and small plates made for sharing, including charcuterie and cheese boards, patatas bravas, seafood, vegetables and more substantial options if you arrive hungry.

This one feels like the perfect October Classy Cocktails night. Crisp fall air, rooftop fire, mountain views, beautiful surroundings, good drinks and a couple of hours hanging out with interesting people.

Come dressed however makes you feel fabulous. Capella may technically lean casual, but I’m just saying... this place can handle a little effort. 😉

Grab a cocktail. Order a few tapas. Pull up a chair by the fire.

We’ll see you nine floors up. 🍸🔥🌆

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Walking Meditation & Qigong
description:
Walking Meditation & Qigong
with Jenne Sluder 
Friday, October 30  |  9 – 10am 
Register Here!
Enjoy a slow, mindful walking meditation through the gardens, practicing breath awareness and sensory attention to touch the deep peace and simple wonders of quiet time in nature. This session begins with a series of gentle and easy Qigong movements to clear the mind, release tension, support the body and brain’s natural healing processes, and generate a sense of inner calm. 
 This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?\*\*
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.

-People under 18 years of age.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision.](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.

Sexual- having or involving sex.

title: Charming Disaster
description:
Kick of Halloween weekend with an extremely special treat, brought to you live here at Jack of the Wood!Brooklyn-based musical duo Charming Disaster was formed in 2012 by Ellia Bisker and Jeff Morris. Inspired by the gothic humor of Edward Gorey and Tim Burton, the murder ballads of the Americana tradition, and the dramatic flair of the cabaret, they write songs that tell stories, using two voices to explore dark narratives and characters with a playfully macabre sensibility.



In their interactive Musical Oracle show, songs are selected by chance by audience members who draw cards from the Charming Disaster Oracle Deck—a Tarot-style divination that straddles the line between concert and theatre. 



Charming Disaster has released seven critically acclaimed albums: Love, Crime & Other Trouble (2015), Cautionary Tales (2017), SPELLS + RITUALS (2019), Our Lady of Radium (2022), Super Natural History (2023), singles collection Time Ghost (2024), and The Double (2025). In their songs, the duo have explored love, death, crime, folklore, mythology, magic, science, and the occult. Their theatrical live performances combine vocal harmonies and clever lyrics with ukulele, guitar, and virtuosic foot percussion, drawing listeners into a spooky, offbeat universe of paranormal romance, con artists, circus performers, ancient mythology, nightclubs, car chases, the afterlife, and beyond. 



Charming Disaster’s music has been featured on the podcast Welcome to Night Vale, they have opened for legendary cello-rock ensemble Rasputina, goth icon Voltaire, and punk cabaret duo The Dresden Dolls, and their theatrical, entertaining live performances have captivated audiences across the United States and Europe. They have played festivals, bars and clubs, museums and art galleries, bookstores and libraries, and the occasional historic cemetery. They have appeared alongside storytellers, comedians, fire eaters, puppets, burlesque artists, poets, and circus performers. Recent appearances include the Meadowlark Festival, the Rochester Fringe Festival, Dragon Con, Joe’s Pub at The Public Theater in NYC, Brooklyn’s historic Green-Wood Cemetery, Philadelphia’s Science History Institute, the Edgar Allan Poe Museum in Richmond, VA, Cleveland’s Wizbang Theatre, and the Coney Island Sideshow stage.Opening will be TOYBOX THEATER: An inexplicable blend of comedy, storytelling, puppetry and clowning with Toybox, America's Favorite Cartoon Witch! Toybox is a multiple award winning artist and has been described as "One of the most unique performers working today". His accolades include, Fan Favorite and Best Performance at the National Puppetry Festival, Funniest and Fringiest at The Asheville Fringe Festival, funding from The Jim Henson Foundation, and an UNIMA Citation of Excellence In The Art of Puppetry, the highest honor given in the field.

title: The Art of Sound Healing
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
We welcome you to Asheville Art Museum to embrace the fullness of the fall season, to turn inward, root into stillness, and shed what no longer serves us. This morning sanctuary at the Museum offers space to rest, quiet the mind, and dream new intentions into existence. We will use breathwork, meditation, and a 50-minute sound bath to let go of old habits, attachments, and grief, and to drop deep into a state of profound, restorative rest. 
Sound baths promote deep release and relaxation, entraining our brainwaves to shift into a dreamlike state. This gentle, grounding practice is open to everybody—no experience needed. Come as you are, tired or wired, or somewhere in between. Please bring a yoga mat or pad, along with anything else to make you comfortable, like cushions and blankets. 
About the Instructor
Timothy Burgin is a world music percussionist who has spent more than 20 years collecting and playing sound healing instruments. A Kripalu & Pranakriya-trained yoga instructor who has lived and taught in Asheville since 2004, he has completed more than 500 hours of yoga training and founded YogaBasics.com. He leads sound baths throughout Asheville, drawing on his training in acupuncture, bodywork, yoga energetics, anatomy, and physiology. 
Register Now 
What are the Benefits to Sound Bowl Healing Music?
Sound bowl healing music involves the use of crystal or Tibetan singing bowls that produce harmonic vibrations. These vibrations are believed to promote deep relaxation, reduce stress, and support emotional and physical healing. The sound frequencies can help align chakras, calm the nervous system, and create a meditative state conducive to mindfulness and inner peace.

title: A Halloween Walk at the John C. Campbell Folk School in Brasstown NC
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The John C. Campbell Folk School is located in Brasstown, Clay County, NC. It has classes in over 50 subjects, including art, craft, dance, music, and nature. (My wife took lap dulcimer lessons there many years ago. A family friend teaches there regularly.) This is the place where John Jacob Niles first performed a song he had collected, "I Wonder as I Wander".

We will gather in the main parking lot of the campus. Our first stop will be at Keith House, where there are restrooms. We will go to the Craft Shop, follow some trails, visit the Herb Garden, see the Eagle Dancer Sculpture, and past a kiln. This is one walk where we will definitely not hesitate to stop and look at various things there are to see. Your camera is a must on this one.

Our route is 5 KM/3.1 miles. Tennis shoes are fine, as there is no significant elevation change. Most will not want walking sticks (although I plan to take one). Bring a protein snack and plenty of water. Wheelchairs might have a somewhat hard time, but trail strollers should be ok. If I remember, dogs would probably be ok.

Before you leave, you may want to pick up lunch at the Folk School. You might bring a picnic lunch from home. Or you might catch some lunch after you have left campus and are on your way home.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Samhain: A Creative Journey through Autumn’s Threshold
description:
Samhaim: A Creative Journey through this Threshold of Autumn
with Catherine Willows 
Saturday, October 31  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
Samhain marks a sacred threshold—the earth releases what is no longer needed, and the Northern Hemisphere begins its descent into the darkness, turning its energy inward toward the stillness of winter to come. We too are invited to slow down, turning our attention toward the transitions and endings that have shaped our lives through this passing year. This is a season of mystery and the unknown, time to discover what may be hidden beneath the surface: deeper knowing, unexpected beauty, new perspectives, and possibilities that have yet to reveal themselves. 
Together, we will attune to Nature and this sacred season within the Arboretum gardens, listen to the deeper rhythms moving through us, and invite our intuition into the creative process. Through expressive artmaking, we will enter this mid-autumn threshold and explore the mystery it holds. Artmaking becomes the portal through which we enter the mystery. Creativity becomes the elixir through which alchemy can open into discovery and transformation. 
No artistic experience is needed, only curiosity, a willingness to listen inwardly, and an openness to discover what reveals itself. If you have a journal, bring that with you to use during the class but all other supplies will be provided. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

Diego Vázquez is a Spanish pianist from Madrid now based in Asheville, NC, who views music as a way to understand and express emotions beyond words. title: 5 KM/3 mile Sunday Afternoon Walk in Canton
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The start/finish point is the parking lot for the Rec Park baseball field (not to be confused with the public-school baseball field next to the football stadium—our meeting place is a little further down the road). The field was destroyed by Hurricane Helene, but has been rebuilt, and the parking area is still there. Hopefully, some of the Clyde Elementary School Cardinals Elite Walking Team and their families will be joining us for this event.

We will start our walk at the Canton Recreation Park, go through part of downtown, up Academy Street, past the historic cemetery and the public library, past Pisgah High School, and back to the start point. The up and down are fairly steep.

Dress appropriately for the weather. Tennis shoes are fine. This is all pavement, but some might want walking sticks for the up and down; I plan to walk with a pair of walking sticks. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs on leash are welcome.

title: South Arts: Southern Circuit Tour of Independent Filmmakers | They Dream
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for a screening of They Dream followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, William D. Caballero. 
After 20 years of chronicling his Puerto Rican family, a director and his mother craft animations that bring their loved ones back to life. 
 
Screening time: 1:26:00 
RESERVE TICKETS NOW 
About the filmmaker:
William D. Caballero is an American filmmaker whose work merges documentary, animation, and handcrafted miniature worlds to explore memory, migration, faith, and the emotional architecture of family. Across film, television, and short-form media, Caballero has developed a singular visual language rooted in tactile set-building, intergenerational storytelling, and a deep reverence for his Puerto Rican heritage. In 2001, he was awarded the prestigious Gates Millennium Scholarship, recognizing his academic promise and leadership at an early stage in his career. Bachelor of Fine Arts from Pratt Institute in 2006 and a Master of Arts from New York University (NYU) in 2008. 
This foundation in both fine art and cinematic storytelling laid the groundwork for a practice that bridges visual art, documentary realism, and experimental fabrication. While at NYU, Caballero created American Dreams Deferred, his first (but not last) autobiographical feature about his family. Caballero first gained widespread recognition in 2015 as the creator of the HBO series Gran’Pa Knows Best, which premiered on HBO and ran for two seasons. Centered on 3D-printed miniature recreations of his Puerto Rican grandfather, the series combined playful scale with emotional depth, redefining what personal storytelling could look like on television. Its inventive approach to memory and intergenerational dialogue positioned Caballero as a bold new voice in hybrid nonfiction storytelling. 
Southern Circuit screenings are funded in part by a grant from South Arts, a regional arts organization, in partnership with the National Endowment for the Arts. For more information about Southern Circuit please visit www.southarts.org/southerncircuit. 
  
Limited capacity—reserve tickets today.

title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, November 3  |  9 – 10:30am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions. 
●  See a full listing of Adult Education Programs at the North Carolina Arboretum here! Questions? Check our FAQs. 
●  We are committed to fostering a diverse, supportive learning community. If the cost of a class is a barrier for you, please complete this scholarship form and we will see what kind of assistance we can provide.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**November 2026 Selection - *Klara and the Sun* by Kazuo Ishiguro**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/059331817X) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/54120408-klara-and-the-sun)

*Here is the story of Klara, an Artificial Friend with outstanding observational qualities, who, from her place in the store, watches carefully the behavior of those who come in to browse, and of those who pass on the street outside. She remains hopeful that a customer will soon choose her. Klara and the Sun is a thrilling book that offers a look at our changing world through the eyes of an unforgettable narrator, and one that explores the fundamental question: what does it mean to love?*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: The Polyvagal Sangha
description:
Inner Peace Collective
**The Polyvagal Sangha**
*A community of seekers exploring nervous system regulation through the lens of ancient wisdom and modern science.*

A new tribe is forming. We're inviting 30 like-minded and like-hearted folks into an ongoing inquiry — learning to cultivate a greater felt sense of calm, ease, safety, and resilience in our bodies, our relationships, and the world around us. The goal isn't just personal regulation, but a ripple effect of co-regulation: a shift in how we show up for others and move through our own lives.

This is the first class in a 3-class series. The whole is greater than the sum of its parts, yet a single dive will yield beneficial results towards salutogenesis.

**Teachers:** Omri Sitton, D.C. and Wills Reed, LCMHCA

**Cost:** $10–$15 suggested donation to local nonprofit *Source Of Wellness*.
\*No one is turned away for lack of funds — all donations are appreciated.

**How to Reserve Your Spot** (please do both — priority goes to folks who complete both steps):

1. **Text Omri at 828-298-0011** with your name and whether you'd like to pay via Venmo or at the door
2. **RSVP on Meetup** using the button on this page

*A note on the two-step process: based on past events, people who only RSVP on Meetup often don't show up. Texting Omri directly helps us plan for who's actually coming — so please do both.*

**A Bit More Detail:**
Polyvagal Theory (PVT) — conceptualized by Stephen Porges — reveals how our body and brain collaborate to respond to everyday stress and deeply held trauma. It highlights the role of the autonomic nervous system, especially the vagus nerve, in shaping our physical and mental health. Paired with mindfulness practices drawn from ancient traditions, PVT offers us both the science and the felt experience of coming back to our center.

By building community together, we naturally stimulate the social engagement system — the nervous system's highest branch — fostering connection, safety, and ease in body, mind, and life. This is the essence of The Polyvagal Sangha.

**Participants will learn:**

* Polyvagal Theory's three defining principles
* Somatic activities specific to each branch of the autonomic nervous system
* Awareness practices to soften emotional triggers and past traumas
* The body's innate biological responses, and the role of mindfulness in being present to "what is"
* How connecting with others committed to personal growth naturally lifts and supports us all

Join Omri and Wills for a series of illustrated, experiential presentations that will inspire your spirit, engage your mind, and challenge your creativity — as you uncover the enormous potential of applying this work in your daily life.

*Feel Well. Heal Well. Live Well.*

**About the teachers:**

**About Omri**
Omri Sitton, D.C., Cert. ZB has 25 years of experience in multiple fields of the healing arts. His passion in helping others has a strong emphasis on self-care.

He naturally weaves the connection between mindfulness practice, cellular consciousness, and polyvagal theory into his experiential classes.

Dr. Omri practices Tonal Chiropractic, Zero Balancing, and Polyvagal Touch in Asheville, offering what he refers to as ChiroSomatics.
Learn more at [omsourcewellness.com](https://www.omsourcewellness.com/)

**About Wills**
Wills Reed, LCMHCA, is an Asheville-based psychotherapist with a particular interest in how our earliest relationships, life experiences, and nervous systems shape the way we experience ourselves and others.

His work draws from attachment-focused therapy, EMDR, somatic approaches, and a longtime personal practice of meditation and contemplative traditions. He enjoys helping people translate these ideas into practical experiences of greater safety, connection, and freedom in everyday life.
